Vector1EcuTetheringHarvestWindowExtracti.description: EQ_01: C_tethered = C_dealer + D_queue * l_daily. A $450.00 independent sensor/actuator fault becomes a $2,250.00 tethered dealer invoice (dealer_software_dispatch_markup_ratio = 2250.0 / 450.0 = 5.0x) plus 4.0 dealer-queue days at $3,500.00/day of critical-harvest-window crop loss ($14,000.00 downtime), for a combined per-fault extraction of $16,250.00 and an enclosure multiplier of round(16250.0 / 450.0, 6) = 36.111111x, of which 0.861538 is unitemized downtime. Hostage dominance: C_dealer + D_queue * l_daily > C_indep.

Vector2GermplasmBiopatentEnclosureRent.description: EQ_02: Rent = (C_trait - C_heirloom) * Acres. A CR4 = 0.85 seed-chemical oligopoly uses utility patents and bag-tag technology licensing agreements (Bowman v. Monsanto Co., 569 U.S. 278 (2013): exhaustion does not extend to reproduction) to outlaw the $28.00/acre saved-heirloom baseline, forcing a $140.00/acre patented trait seed + tied herbicide repurchase every spring (seed_trait_enclosure_markup_ratio = 140.0 / 28.0 = 5.0x), extracting ($140.00 - $28.00) * 1,000 = $112,000.00/yr per 1,000-acre family farm and $3,360,000.00 over a 30-year horizon, with CR4 = 0.85 above the 0.50 high-concentration benchmark.

Vector3MilkovichFalsificationAndBareMeta.description: EQ_03: Milkovich disclosed-facts synthesis. The H0 emissions/safety and R&D defenses are falsified by the FTC complaint's non-emissions lock coverage (seat switches, grain-tank augers), the 17 U.S.C. Sec. 1201 triennial agricultural-equipment repair exemptions (granted 2018; renewed 2021 and 2024), and Impression Products, Inc. v. Lexmark International, Inc., 581 U.S. 360 (2017) (authorized sale exhausts patent rights; post-sale servitudes unenforceable). Open ISO 11783 (ISOBUS) / SAE J1939 buses with owner-flashed ECU firmware drive M_enclosure to 1.0x; public-domain land-grant germplasm with legal saved seed drives R_annual to $0.00.

dmca_agricultural_repair_exemption_scope.const: Triennial Librarian of Congress rulemaking exemption permitting circumvention of technological protection measures on agricultural equipment firmware for good-faith diagnosis, maintenance, and repair (granted 2018; renewed 2021 and 2024).

impression_products_pin_cite.const: Impression Products, Inc. v. Lexmark International, Inc., 581 U.S. 360 (2017)

patent_exhaustion_identity.const: Authorized Sale => Patent Rights Exhausted; Post-Sale Servitude Enforceability = 0

h0_null_hypothesis_oem_position.const: OEM position: cryptographic ECU locks prevent EPA emissions tampering and safety hazards, and the 2023 American Farm Bureau Federation MOU already grants repair access. Seed-conglomerate position: trait royalties fund drought-tolerance and yield R&D whose benefits flow back to farmers.

h1_falsification_disclosed_facts.const: As pleaded in FTC v. Deere (No. 3:25-cv-50017), lock coverage extends to non-emissions components (seat switches, grain-tank augers, ordinary sensors); the Librarian of Congress granted 17 U.S.C. Sec. 1201 agricultural-equipment repair exemptions (2018, renewed 2021 and 2024) finding no copyright impairment; and Impression Products, 581 U.S. 360 (2017), holds that an authorized sale exhausts patent rights, rendering post-sale servitudes unenforceable. Bowman survives only at the reproduction boundary, which public-domain germplasm sidesteps entirely.
